## Project Description

This experiment examines how exposure to microplastics levels affect the
thermal limit (Critical Thermal Maximum; CTmax) and acclimation capacity
of Skistodiaptomus pallidus (S. pallidus) under ambient and elevated
temperature conditions relevant to heatwave predictions.

We will use a factorial design and a one week treatment period, with
groups exposed to control conditions (16°C, No microplastics), a
microplastics treatment (16°C with microplastics), a heatwave treatment
(22°C and no microplastics), and a combined treatment with both
microplastics and heatwave conditions. Results will improve our
understanding of copepod resilience in a warming, plastic-polluted world
by XYZ.

## Questions, Objectives, Hypotheses

Questions:

1.  How does exposure to end-of-century concentrations of MPs affect the
    thermal tolerance of S. pallidus?

2.  Do MPs affect S. pallidus ability to acclimate to end-of-century
    heatwave temperatures?

Hypotheses:

1.  Exposure to end-of-century concentrations of MPs will cause an
    increase in thermal tolerance because of stress pathways are
    activated by the MPs, priming organisms to respond to thermal
    stress.
2.  MPs will increase S. pallidus's acclimation ability to
    end-of-century heatwave temperatures.

## Study Design

**Comment: This section needs to be completed and cleaned up.**

Species: Skistodiaptomus pallidus

Cultures: Centennial Park; Lowell Canal if extended

Generation: F\>3

Treatments: 16C (Control), 22C (Heatwave)

MP Treatments: None, Present **Comment: We need a target concentration
of microplastics (Undecided)**

Trait Measurement: CTmax

Animals/dish: 14 (per equation: Animals/dish = ((# assays × \# tubes)/#
dishes) + (0.5 × \# assays))

Dishes per treatment per replicate: 1 (4 dishes total: N+C, N+W, MP+C,
MP+W)

Total animals needed per experimental replicate: 56

CTmax measurements per treatment per replicate: 12 (3 animals × 4
assays)

Experimental replicates: 3

Total CTmax measurements per treatment (across study): 36

Total animals needed (across study): 168

1.  Animals are collected from field and brought to lab.
2.  On setup day X adult females are selected from the lab culture and
    are evenly split into four different dishes with XmL of DIO and
    \~0.5mL-1.5mL C. ozolini.
3.  By the end of setup there will be four dishes: N+C, N+W, MP+C, MP+W,
    and each dish will have X animals. Equation used to get \#
    animals/dish: Animals/dish = ((# of assays \* \# of tubes)/# of
    dishes) + (0.5 \* \# of assays) **Comment: Initial CTmax
    measurements?**
4.  Dishes are given their respective amounts of MPs.
5.  Each dish is placed into their respective incubators, a temperature
    sensor is also placed in the incubators in a dish with 150mL of tap
    water to closely monitor the internal temperatures of the incubators
    (in the incubator there are two shelves, the temperature treatments
    are always on the same shelf as one another but alternate every
    replicate, also the incubator that is used as the control or the
    warm alternates every replicate).
6.  On day 7, 4 CTmax assays are ran using 2-3 animals from each dish in
    each assay. Tube placements for each assay are randomized using
    Skisto_LARA/Scripts/00_tube_assignments.R
7.  After every CTmax image and record each copepod.
8.  The entire experiment is replicated 3 times.

```{mermaid}
    B --> C[Split evenly into 4 dishes:<br>N+C, N+W, MP+C, MP+W<br>+ X mL DIO + 0.5-1.5mL C. ozolini]
    C --> D[MP dishes given<br>microplastic treatment]
    D --> E[Dishes placed in incubators<br>16°C or 22°C<br>+ temp sensor dish]
    E --> F[Acclimation period:<br>Day 0 - Day 7]
    F --> G[Day 7: 4 CTmax assays run<br>2-3 animals from each dish per assay<br>tube placement randomized]
    G --> H[Image and record<br>each copepod post-CTmax]
    H --> I{Repeat entire<br>experiment}
    I -->|3 experimental replicates| B
    
```

## Statistics

### Data Processing

Data is processed by controller scripts: acc_hours is defined,
calculated from Acclimation Day and Start Time treatment_group is
defined by combining Temperature Treatment and Microplastic Treatment
(N+C, N+W, MP+C, MP+W)

### Statistical Tests of Hypotheses

Hypothesis 1:

-   Tests of assumptions: Exposure to end-of-century concentrations of
    MPs will cause an increase in thermal tolerance because of stress
    pathways are activated by the MPs, priming organisms to respond to
    thermal stress. Statistical model: Temperature Treatment × MP
    Treatment

-   How model fit will be evaluated: Using the performance package in R

-   Post-hoc tests: The CTmax of the no-MP and MP-present groups will be
    compared at each acclimation temperature. Support for this
    hypothesis would appear as consistently higher CTmax in MP-present
    animals.

-   Caveats/Caution when interpreting results: This design is limited to
    two stressors, other potentially interacting factors (e.g., food
    availability, oxygen levels, pollutants) are not accounted for and
    could influence thermal tolerance in ways this experiment cannot
    detect. (specify where that might be a problem)

-   Handling missing values: Any missing values will not be included in
    final data.

Hypothesis 2:

-   Tests of assumptions: MPs will increase S. pallidus's acclimation
    ability to end-of-century heatwave temperatures.

-   How model fit will be evaluated: Using the performance package in R

-   Post-hoc tests: Comparing the change in CTmax across the acclimation
    period between MP-present and MP-absent animals within the warm
    (22°C) treatment (i.e., N+W vs. MP+W)

-   Caveats/Caution when interpreting results: Moving animals between
    dishes/tubes on setup day and assay day could stress them slightly,
    which may lower or raise their measured CTmax independent of MP
    exposure.

-   Handling missing values: Missing values will be excluded from
    analysis, this hypothesis relies on comparisons across the
    acclimation period.
